inspection_summary: All 1,924 Python splitlines were inspected against the normalized text. The article proves the leading short-interval maximum scale by combining a Sobolev/second-moment upper bound with a lower-bound transfer from critical-line zeta values to mollified short-prime Dirichlet polynomials, then a log-correlated/branching-style large-deviation and second-moment argument. Prose is coherent throughout; displayed formulas have text-layer fragmentation, so formula-dependent units are retained only where the checked prose fixes the mechanism and are flagged for equation-level scan verification.

within_source_synthesis_candidates.title: Log-correlated structure as the reason to coarse-grain
within_source_synthesis_candidates.claim: The logarithmic covariance picture is operationalized, not merely analogical: prime-size blocks act as scales, point separation determines how many scales remain shared, and pair-tail estimates retain exactly that multiscale dependence.
within_source_synthesis_candidates.limit: The source establishes this mechanism for its chosen prime-polynomial decomposition and fixed coarse graining; it does not prove a general universality theorem for all log-correlated fields.

within_source_synthesis_candidates.title: A modular zeta-to-prime-polynomial transfer stack
within_source_synthesis_candidates.claim: The lower bound is factored into separately controlled representation changes: shift off the critical line, invert zeta typically with a mollifier, make that control uniform locally, replace the mollifier by an exponential of logarithmic prime blocks, and transfer a block high point back to zeta.
within_source_synthesis_candidates.limit: Every transition is typical/probabilistic and quantitative; the chain is not a pointwise identity and depends on discarding exceptional blocks and sets.

within_source_synthesis_candidates.title: From diagonal moments to existence of an extreme point
within_source_synthesis_candidates.claim: Diagonal mean values generate approximate Gaussian moments; a cutoff makes moment-to-transform passage safe; transform inversion yields one- and two-point tails; a near/far pair decomposition then turns those local distributional facts into existence of a high mesh point.
within_source_synthesis_candidates.limit: The conclusion is leading-order and tied to the stated transform ranges, mesh, fixed K, and text's error estimates; formula-level constants require scan verification.
